claim: The production destructive gate is complete only when `universe_authoritative` is true, `frontier_namespaces > 0`, and `frontier_proven == frontier_namespaces`; `suppress_destructive` is then `!report.anomalies.empty() || !carried_holds.empty() || frontier_incomplete`.

In `planManifestCursorPage`, `catalog_recovery_authoritative` controls only whether debris for a catalog-named namespace may be recovered; recovery still requires `prefixEligible`, refuses `Creating`, handles protection-view exceptions, and checks active keys before nomination.

At the destructive gate call site, `!suppress_destructive` implies `frontier_complete`, which implies `universe_authoritative`; therefore `planManifestCursorPage` receives an authoritative recovery argument whenever the gate opens.

The frozen-tail exit, `FrontierUnproven::NoCatalogEntry`, `no_catalog_entry`, `AppendAboveFrozenTail`, `append_above_frozen_tail`, and `WalkTarget::frozen_tail` were removed because their guards are structurally dead; the absent-record branch now keeps the stricter hold behavior.

`FrontierDeficit::count` is called once for each namespace with `frontier_proven == false`, so the frontier-deficit buckets sum to `frontier_namespaces - frontier_proven`; `probe_budget` and `fold_aborted` are counted outside the namespace loop.

Every non-proven frontier exit identifies a cause through `CheckpointUnusable`, `CheckpointFrontierEmpty`, `CommittedBelowCursor`, or a held/fired walk path, so `FrontierDeficit::unattributed` is structurally zero for the current walk.

`CasListLiarEndToEnd.AnEntirelyHiddenNamespacesEdgeIsRefusedByTheProductionDefault` does not test the claimed member-count frontier failure because `buildKillShot` writes no `_ckpt` for either namespace; both namespaces instead take the `checkpoint_unusable` anomaly path, so the test would pass even if the universe term were removed.

`CasGcFrontierGate.HiddenPlusOneInAnUnknownNamespaceIsRefusedByTheProductionDefault` asserts `frontier_complete == true` and `suppress_destructive == false`, so its name and section header misdescribe the behavior it verifies.

The five destructive suppressor families are tested separately: healthy operation, explicit negative policy, anomaly, carried hold, empty-universe floor, and exhausted probe budget; `expectEveryDeleteFamilyInert` checks blobs, `/cas/manifests/`, `/gc/gen/`, `/cas/ns/stream/`, and the total.

The T8 healthy-pool soak should check zero `no usable checkpoint` anomalies in addition to zero `unproven` and zero frontier-probe budget, because a namespace with no usable checkpoint now suppresses through an anomaly rather than silently.

Inside the ref-walk loop, `grounding` is non-null and the first ceiling test compares `expected` with `*grounding->committed_through`; after the ceiling and crossing paths, the loop body always satisfies `*expected <= *grounding->committed_through`.

The ref-walk frontier is finite because `committed_through` is a round-start snapshot, and a namespace cannot enter the walk with an empty `grounding` or empty `grounding->committed_through` optional.

`FoldResult::FrontierUnproven` records a reason per unproven namespace, while `FoldResult::FrontierDeficit` exposes nine counters and `count`/`total`/`describe` helpers; suppression logs append an `unproven:` clause when the deficit is nonzero.
The frontier instrumentation adds no backend requests; its normal per-namespace cost is one `uint8_t` store, and formatting occurs only inside the already-suppressed path when the deficit is nonzero.

A namespace can leave the old walk silent when `cursor == RefTxnId{}`, `listing.logs` is empty, and `checkpoints.life_epochs` has no entry; the old code skipped `while (expected)` with no anomaly, hold, or warning, while the current `!grounding` arm emits a warning and records `CheckpointUnusable` or a hold.

The T6a artifact's enumeration of silent frontier exits was incomplete because it omitted the walk-that-never-started shape; a `Removing` row with a reclaimed `_ckpt`, a decoded checkpoint without `life_epoch`, or the test-only `casAdmitEntry` bridge can produce that shape.

The `FrontierDeficit` documentation should be attached to `struct FrontierDeficit` rather than `enum class FrontierUnproven`, because the bucket contract describes the former and is surfaced under the wrong symbol.

The `checkpoint_unusable` frontier bucket counts only the no-cursor variant; when an unreadable checkpoint has a cursor, the effective-hold site overwrites the reason with `Held`, while the warning and seal still retain the underlying `CheckpointUndecodable` cause.
`gc_round_graduation_budget` and `gc_round_redelete_budget` are `UInt64` settings with default `5000`; `0` means unbounded, and matching fields are carried through `PoolConfig`.

When the graduation or redelete budget is exhausted, `settleEntry` carries the entry in `still_retired` unchanged: a condemned entry remains condemned, and a `delete_pending` entry remains `delete_pending` for a later round.

One `GcRoundWorkBudget` is constructed per round in `Gc::runRegularRound` and shared by sequential shard folds; it is passed to all production `foldDeltasIntoGeneration` calls, while the rebuild path remains unbudgeted because it has no graduation or `delete_pending` inputs.
`gc_round_sweep_namespace_budget` defaults to `20` and `gc_round_sweep_recovery_op_budget` defaults to `5000`; both use `0` for unbounded work.

`planManifestCursorPage` freezes at most `nomination_budget` well-formed candidates before performing exact GETs; a well-formed key beyond the cap is retained with `budget_exhausted` instead of reaching the old `chassert`.

If the namespace fan-out or recovery-operation budget is exhausted, `activeManifestKeys` marks `NamespaceProtection::recovery_incomplete`, and the planner discards partial protection sets and retains every candidate in that namespace under `SweepRetainClass::WorkBudgetExhausted`.

`recoverRefTableDetailedFromAuthority` is deliberately not internally budgeted because `fsck` and the GC rebuild path require a complete table; only the committed-tail walk owned by the orphan planner is capped, with the shared recovery call counted as one coarse operation.

Every candidate visited by the orphan planner is either nominated or retained with `decided_through` advanced; the only non-advancing path is nomination-budget exhaustion, which always allows the first well-formed key through when `nomination_budget >= 1`.
`gc_round_ref_cleanup_budget` defaults to `5000` and `gc_round_prefix_wholesale_budget` defaults to `20000`; `0` means unbounded for both settings.

`deletePrefixWholesale` reports `out_fully_drained = true` only when the LIST reaches its natural end; budget exhaustion reports false, and `pruneSupersededGenerations` advances `snap_pruned_through` only past fully drained prefixes.

`cleanupRefObjects` applies a cumulative `GcRoundWorkBudget` cap immediately before each `deleteRefObject`; `deleteRefObject` keeps its per-key catalog-cut and `gc/state` lease validation unchanged, and excess candidates are recomputed from durable state on the next round.
The post-CAS generation-prefix hand-off uses a separate budget from ordinary prune work because it is a one-shot event whose only existing backstop after a partial reclaim is `fsck`.
`gc_round_outcome_entry_budget` defaults to `5000` and caps the cumulative number of `OutcomeEntry` rows appended across redelete and spared loops in one round; `0` is unbounded.

The outcome-entry cap limits only the `GcOutcomes` audit-log PUT: `settleEntry` still removes spared entries from `still_retired`, and `CasGcRetiredSpared`, `GcRecheckVerdict`, and `forgetCondemnMarker` run even when the `OutcomeEntry` push is skipped.
`gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` defaults to `5000` and limits the `manifest_deletes` phase; exhaustion records `skipped_budget` and leaves the undeleted manifests for a later reclaimer.

`folded.mf_cleanup` is one-shot rather than durable across GC rounds: the same round advances the ref-log cursor past the owner-removal transaction before `manifest_deletes`, so budget-declined manifests are reclaimed by the orphan-manifest sweep instead of being reintroduced by the next fold.
`gc_round_handoff_prefix_wholesale_budget` defaults to `5000` and is stored separately from the prune-only `gc_round_prefix_wholesale_budget`; its budget is consumed by the post-CAS hand-off reclaim.
The round-budget implementation introduces no persisted object kinds and no protocol-step changes; the budget is stack-local, and the one-pass round still commits `gc/state` exactly once.

On budget exhaustion, every T6b work family fails closed: graduation and redelete entries remain in `still_retired`, sweep candidates remain in `cas/manifests/`, ref objects remain durable, and a partially drained generation leaves the prune cursor before that generation.
The retained-byte axis of T6-1 remains unbounded: limiting retained manifest bodies to at most `nomination_budget` objects still permits roughly 25 GiB when valid manifests can reach 256 MiB each.
`gc_round_sweep_namespace_budget = 20` should be observed in T8 soak testing because it is a per-round throughput limit that can retain namespaces when more than 20 debris namespaces share one page.

The four token-diff model configurations `stage5_tokendiff`, `sab_skipchangedshard`, `sab_skipparksdeadprecommit`, and `fix_skipparksdeadprecommit` were retired because no production seam skips a manifest or owner-transition fold read based on a LIST-derived token match.
The landed ref-log intake keeps the exact-key `GET` at `cursor + 1` unconditional even when the listed tail equals the cursor, because that read is what establishes `frontier_proven`.
The `CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore` model retains two named debts: Phase-4 sharding is unproven, and `stage5_lazytrim` is unproven by timeout after the extended bound.

The `CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore` `live` configuration reached `74,147,107` generated and `17,845,340` distinct states, while `stage5_lazytrim` reached `1,333,723,653` generated and `233,198,128` distinct states before timing out with `24,395,446` queued.

`RefPlan::changedRows` and `shouldDeferRound` can defer an entire fold round based on a listed tail observation, but the defer path performs no destructive work, advances no coverage cursor, and is bounded by `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds`.
`Gc::newestFoldSealRef` uses listing absence as a virgin-by-enumeration verdict on the rebuild path, and this is documented as a named residual through `RebuildReport::virgin_by_enumeration`.

`GReclaimDeadPrecommit` and `LiveDeadPrecommitReclaimed` are now inert model artifacts because GC-side abandoned-precommit reclaim was removed; the production writer appends the exact `owner_transition` removal instead.

`docs/superpowers/cas/06-tla-models.md` still describes `Gc::computeDiscoverDecisions`, `ShardCoverage`, `CasGcPrecommitRevisitForced`, and `min_live_precommit_*` as a landed fix even though those seams and fields were deleted; it also names deleted `stage5_tokendiff` and skip-precommit configs.

The pinned TLC runner classifier accepts both `Temporal properties were violated` and `Temporal property <Name> was violated` forms, and the latter singular form is emitted by the pinned `TLC2 Version 2026.07.18.145032` jar for a single `PROPERTY`.

The four T7 Lane B model runners are pinned with `check_tlc_pin`, use TLC `2026.07.18.145032` revision `30cc360`, and require SHA-256 `cc4803dce2a8ffaf0f5920a9dc39df4b5ee34ab4cb53fb58ac557277a7e516b3` for `tla2tools.jar`.

The `CaGcDestructiveGateCore` model pins `UniverseAuthoritative == TRUE` because it models the post-flip posture; production's not-yet-knowable-universe posture suppresses destructive work and is covered by `CasGcFrontierGate.HiddenPlusOneInAnUnknownNamespaceIsRefusedByTheProductionDefault`.

The T7 model runner treats a temporal violation as valid only when the log names the expected property and the config contains a singular `PROPERTY` line; a different property or plural `PROPERTIES` config falls through to failure.
The renamed system-table pages are `cas_gc_log.md`, `cas_log.md`, and `cas_mounts.md`, with slugs under `/operations/system-tables/cas_*` and explicit anchors on every touched heading.

The CAS storage settings in `ContentAddressedSettings::loadFromConfig` are direct children of the disk element: the loader calls `config.keys(config_prefix, ...)` and reads `config_prefix + "." + key`, so a nested `<content_addressed>` settings block is not part of the configuration contract.
The documented CAS configuration example uses only keys registered in `LIST_OF_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_SETTINGS`; the checked example contained no unregistered CAS setting names.

The user-facing disk commands are `cas-fsck`, `cas-gc-dryrun`, `cas-gc-rebuild`, `cas-inspect`, and `cas-drop-member`; the deprecated `fsck` alias and `CommandFsckDeprecated` factory and registration were removed, while C++ class names such as `CommandCaInspect` were retained.
`clickhouse disks --query 'help'` lists the five `cas-*` commands and no `fsck`; querying `fsck` exits 36 and prints the available-command listing.

`utils/ca-soak/scenarios/tests/test_render_tuned_config.py` was a red test because it still expected `<metadata_type>content_addressed</metadata_type>` after the setting value changed to `cas`; the assertion was corrected to `cas`.
`utils/ca-soak/scripts/soak_watch.sh` still issued `SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS content_addressed_log`, but that table no longer exists after the CAS naming change.

The current CAS metadata type is `cas`; the old `content_addressed` value, old config filename `content_addressed_*.xml`, and old stateless prefixes `content_addressed` and `ca_gc` are retired in favor of `cas_*`.
`CasObjectPut` has never existed in `src/Common/ProfileEvents.cpp`; the soak query's `CasObjectPut` alternative was removed, leaving the working `CASBlobPut` metric name unchanged.

The planned `Cas[A-Z]` cleanup gate was invalid because it passed a PCRE lookahead to `grep -vE`, which does not support lookahead and could report zero lines after an error; a Python classifier was required for the actual sweep.

The persisted fold-seal serialization key `gen` remains unchanged in `Formats/CasFoldSealFormat.cpp` and its golden test; `gc/gen/*` is likewise a persisted object-key path, not a renameable user-facing abbreviation.

`MountLease` fields and related `system.cas_log` detail keys retain `started_at_ms` and `expires_at_ms` because their values are raw epoch milliseconds; the suffix is semantically accurate even where a display column uses `DateTime64(3)`.

Short `CasEvent::detail` keys `ns`, `me`, `p`, and `ha` remain in `CasFsck` and `CasGc` report maps because they were outside the decided rename list; they require a separate naming decision before any rewrite.

`CatalogLifecycleReconciler::reconcile` selects an eligible completed-removal row before applying the component-level clean-return fence; an eligible row always calls `CasRefCatalog::deleteCompletedRemovingAtSnapshot`, and a fence loss resolves that exact row as `ExactRowStillPresent`.

`DrainComplete` is reserved for a catalog cut with no eligible completed-removal row; an eligible row cannot return `{FencedOut, DrainComplete}` because selection precedes the mandatory resolution cut.

`seedCompletedRemoving` recovers and retains the predecessor runtime while its catalog row is `Live`; absent and replacement fence-race fixtures therefore exercise real `Pool::invalidateRemovedCatalogLife` behavior and force name-based recovery away from the predecessor life.

The reconciler's eligible-row path performs the initial selection `GET` and the primitive's mandatory resolution `GET`, without adding another catalog read; a genuinely clean no-eligible cut retains its component-level fence check before returning the final snapshot.
